title: ‘I am trapped here’: Gulf-based Nepali workers agonise as devastating floods ravage home - Middle East Eye
description: ‘I am trapped here’: Gulf-based Nepali workers agonise as devastating floods ravage home  Middle East Eye
publisher.title: Middle East Eye
full_article:
Under Dubai’s blinding afternoon sun, Hari Krishna lays bricks for a luxury residential complex.

But his thoughts are 2,000 miles away, amid the mud and debris of Nepal’s Bhote Khosi-Trishuli corridor.

For the past week, the 32-year-old construction worker, who sends most of his earnings home, has spent every spare minute frantically trying to call his relatives on iMO and checking local news channels on his cracked smartphone.

Late August brought catastrophic flash floods to his home district of Nuwakot in Nepal. The waters swept away bridges, roads, and entire hillside settlements, leaving at least 1,399 people dead across the country and nearly 5,400 missing at the time of writing.

And like thousands of Nepalis, the floods swept away everything Krishna’s family owned - their house, household supplies, money, gold and a shed housing their cows and goats. With their land destroyed, Krishna said there is no possibility of farming in the future.

The disaster struck his hometown in the Bidur Municipality of Nuwakot District, claiming the life of his 67-year-old grandfather.

“I planned to visit my family for the upcoming Dashain festival, but that wish will now be unfulfilled with my grandfather gone,” Krishna told Middle East Eye, his voice trembling as he thought about the loss his family have experienced.

“My family is sleeping in a holding centre, terrified of the next landslide, and planning my grandfather’s final death rites.

Police conduct search and rescue operations in Trishuli, in Nepal's Nuwakot district, on 7 September 2026 after the flash floods in August (Pedro Pardo/AFP)

“I asked my supervisor for emergency leave, but I don’t have the money for a sudden flight, and even if I did, the roads to my village are completely washed out.

“It would have been better if I was home and killed by the flood. I am trapped here.”

Krishna’s plight is echoed across the Gulf, where hundreds of thousands of Nepali migrants work to support their families back home. The glittering skylines of Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia have been built largely by South Asian labour.

Now, as Nepal faces one of its most catastrophic climate disasters in recent history, the burden of rebuilding will inevitably fall on these same workers.

Nepal relies heavily on its diaspora, with remittances accounting for roughly a third of its gross domestic product; remittances from the Gulf, according to the Nepal Rastra Bank, account for 40 per cent of all Nepali remittances.

'A systematic horror'

UN agencies like the International Labour Organisation (ILO) note that extreme crises highlight how precarious the situation is for these workers.

Across the migration cycle, Nepali labourers face immense risks, from their wages being withheld to limited access to healthcare.

Rameshwar Nepal, an investigator for Equidem, a global human and labour rights organisation, said many Nepali workers are desperate to leave but face overwhelming logistical hurdles.

“They are thousands of miles away [in the Gulf], while their families and communities face the devastation at home,” Nepal told MEE from Kathmandu, where he is coordinating relief efforts for workers and their families.

“They desperately want to return home and be with their families, see if they are still alive, and see the state of their homes, properties, relatives and communities for themselves.”

Damaged houses in the aftermath of the flash floods that devastated Trishuli in Nepal's Nuwakot district on 6 September 2026 (Pedro Pardo/AFP)

But the journey back is laced with fear and uncertainty about whether they can return to work in the Gulf.

“They don’t know whether they will be allowed to go, whether they will get paid leave, or, even if they are willing to go on unpaid leave, whether they will be allowed to do so,” Nepal explained.

Beyond securing permission and covering flight costs, workers fear the long-term impact on their livelihoods.

“Many of them need these jobs, particularly if they have lost their homes and property in the disaster. They need to know that they will still have a job to return to.”

Nepal pointed out that the region's labour sponsorship framework exacerbates this immobility, comparing the current anxiety to the Covid-19 lockdowns.

“The kafala system, which is a systematic kind of horror for migrant workers in terms of their freedom of mobility, is pertinent even in difficult situations like this,” he noted.

“We saw a similar situation back in 2020... They really wanted to return to their families, but they were prevented from doing so. It sounds like a very inhuman type of situation.”

'Starting from Zero'

In Qatar, 37-year-old driver Shiva Ujjwal is living that exact nightmare.

Ujjwal has spent the last three years driving workers from the labour camps housing thousands of cleaners and construction workers on the outskirts of Doha to offices and building sites dotted across the Gulf capital.

The driver was starting his early morning shift when disaster struck. Without a chance to check social media, he first heard the news from fellow workers.

When his supervisor allowed him to use his phone, his frantic calls home failed - the communication networks in the region had been completely cut off.

“My heart was breaking,” Ujjwal said, recalling the first time he saw the devastating videos online.

A woman looks at photographs outside a morgue in Kathmandu on 7 September following the flash floods that swept through Nepal's Nuwakot district (Pedro Pardo/AFP)

“From the scale of the flood, I could easily imagine my house had been taken away, but I was very worried about my family.”

While his wife, children, and parents managed to escape safely, the human toll around them was staggering. Nine of his relatives were killed, and countless others from his village remain missing.

“My family members ran with empty hands, with no chance to take important papers, money, or gold,” he explained.

“We lost all our property in less than five seconds by a single hit of a live-bullet-type flood.”

Burden of rebuilding

For Ujjwal, who previously worked in Saudi Arabia and the UAE before moving to Qatar three years ago, the material loss represents years of erased labour.

He had painstakingly built his family’s home in phases over several years, using his modest savings to fund one floor at a time. Though his Gulf wages were modest, the opportunity helped “light his kitchen” and keep his family afloat. Now, he faces the daunting prospect of starting from zero.

'We lost all our property in less than five seconds by a single hit of a live-bullet-type flood' - Shiva Ujjwal, Nepalese worker in Qatar

His supervisor is arranging to send him back to Nepal on unpaid leave, but the geographic and emotional distance has taken a heavy toll, especially during the initial multi-day communication blackout.

“It is very stressful to stay here as my family is in a holding centre now,” he said, burdened by the thought of how to eventually rebuild their home. “My body is here, but I am not here.”

For the Nepali diaspora in the Gulf, the immediate response has been mobilisation. Grassroots fundraising campaigns are circulating through WhatsApp groups as workers pool their meagre savings to send bulk relief to the hardest-hit districts.

Yet, for men like Ujjwal and Krishna, the financial support feels like a hollow substitute for being home.

दुबई केरऽ दुपहर केरऽ आँखऽ वाला रौद के नीचे हरि कृष्ण एगो लग्जरी आवासीय परिसर लेली ईंट बिछाबै छै ।

मुदा हुनक विचार 2000 मील दूर, नेपालक भोटे खोसी-त्रिशुली गलियाराक थाल-कादो आ मलबा के बीच अछि.

पिछला एक सप्ताह स 32 वर्षीय निर्माण मजदूर जे अपन कमाई क अधिकांश हिस्सा घर पठा दैत छथि, हर खाली मिनट उन्माद मे अपन रिश्तेदार कए आईएमओ पर फोन करबाक आ अपन दरार पड़ल स्मार्टफोन पर स्थानीय न्यूज चैनल चेक करबा मे बिता रहल छथि।

अगस्त के अंत मे नेपाल के हुनकर गृह जिला नुवाकोट मे विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि आबि गेल छल. ई पानी पुल, सड़क आरू पूरा पहाड़ी के ढाल वाला बस्ती क॑ बहाय देलकै, जेकरा स॑ ई खबर लिखै के समय देश भर म॑ कम स॑ कम १३९९ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै आरू लगभग ५,४०० लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलै ।

आ हजारो नेपाली जकाँ बाढ़ि मे कृष्णक परिवारक सभ किछु - घर, घरक सामान, पाइ, सोना आ गाय-बकरीक रहबाक एकटा शेड बहरा गेल | हुनकर जमीन नष्ट भेला स कृष्ण कहला जे भविष्य मे खेती क कोनो संभावना नहि अछि।

नयका एमईई न्यूजलेटर: जेरुसलम डिस्पैच टर्की अनपैक्ड आरू अन्य एमईई न्यूजलेटर के साथ-साथ इजरायल-फिलिस्तीन के बारे म॑ नवीनतम अंतर्दृष्टि आरू विश्लेषण लेली साइन अप करलऽ जाय

नुवाकोट जिल्लाके बिदुर नगरपालिकामे हुनकर सासुरमे ई आपदामे ६७ वर्षीय दादाके जान गेल ।

कृष्णा न॑ मिडिल ईस्ट आई क॑ कहलकै कि आबै वाला दशैन महोत्सव लेली हम्में अपनऽ परिवार स॑ मिलै के योजना बनयने छेलियै, लेकिन वू इच्छा अब॑ अधूरा होय जैतै, जब॑ हुनी अपनऽ परिवार क॑ करलऽ गेलऽ नुकसान के बारे म॑ सोचतें हुअ॑ आवाज काँपतें हुअ॑ मिडिल ईस्ट आई क॑ कहलकै ।

“हमर परिवार एकटा होल्डिंग सेंटर मे सुतल अछि, अगिला भूस्खलन सँ आतंकित अछि, आ हमर दादाजी’क अंतिम मृत्यु संस्कार’क योजना बना रहल अछि.

नेपालके नुवाकोट जिल्लाके त्रिशुलीमे अगस्तमे भेल आकस्मिक बाढिक बाद ७ सितम्बर २०२६के पुलिस खोजबीन आ बचाव अभियान चलाओल गेल (पेड्रो पारदो/एएफपी)

ओ कहलनि जे, हम अपन सुपरवाइजर स’ इमरजेंसी लीव मंगलहुं, मुदा अचानक फ्लाइट’क पाइ नहि अछि, आ जँ भेटल त’ हमर गाम’क सड़क पूरा तरहे बहल अछि.

“घर मे रहितहुँ आ बाढ़ि मे मरि गेल रहैत त’ नीक रहैत, हम एतहि फँसल छी।”

कृष्ण केरऽ दुर्दशा पूरा खाड़ी म॑ गूंजी रहलऽ छै, जहां लाखों नेपाली प्रवासी घर वापसी म॑ अपनऽ परिवार केरऽ भरण पोषण लेली काम करै छै । कतर, संयुक्त अरब अमीरात आरू सऊदी अरब केरऽ चमकैतऽ क्षितिज केरऽ निर्माण बहुत हद तलक दक्षिण एशियाई मजदूरऽ द्वारा करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

आब नेपाल के हाल के इतिहास में अपन एकटा विनाशकारी जलवायु आपदा के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि, पुनर्निर्माण के बोझ अनिवार्य रूप सं एही मजदूर पर पड़त.

नेपाल अपन प्रवासी पर बेसी निर्भर अछि, जकर सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के लगभग एक तिहाई हिस्सा रेमिटंस अछि; खाड़ीसँ प्रेषण नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकके अनुसार सभ नेपाली प्रेषणमे ४० प्रतिशत अछि ।

'एक व्यवस्थित भयावहता'।

अंतर्राष्ट्रीय श्रम संगठन (आईएलओ) जैसनऽ संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एजेंसी नोट करै छै कि चरम संकट ई बात क॑ रेखांकित करै छै कि ई मजदूरऽ लेली स्थिति कतनी अनिश्चित छै ।

पलायन चक्र के पार नेपाली मजदूर के मजदूरी रोकला सं ल क स्वास्थ्य सेवा के सीमित पहुंच तक अपार जोखिम के सामना करय पड़ैत अछि.

वैश्विक मानव आ मजदूर अधिकार संगठन एक्वीडेम के अन्वेषक रामेश्वर नेपाल कहलनि जे, बहुतो नेपाली मजदूर छोड़य लेल बेताब छथि मुदा रसद के भारी बाधा के सामना करय पड़ैत अछि।

नेपाल न॑ काठमांडू स॑ एमईई स॑ बातचीत म॑ कहलकै कि हुनी हजारों मील दूर [खाड़ी म॑] छै, जबकि हुनकऽ परिवार आरू समुदाय क॑ घरऽ म॑ ही तबाही के सामना करना पड़ै छै ।

“ओ सब बेताब चाहैत छथि जे घर घुरि क’ अपन परिवारक संग रहू, देखू जे ओ एखनो जीवित छथि कि नहि, आ अपन घर, संपत्ति, रिश्तेदार आ समुदायक स्थिति स्वयं देखथि।”

नेपालक नुवाकोट जिलामे ६ सितम्बर २०२६ केँ त्रिशूली केँ तबाह करयवला आकस्मिक बाढ़िक बाद क्षतिग्रस्त घर (पेड्रो पारदो/एएफपी)

लेकिन वापसी के यात्रा में डर आरू अनिश्चितता के फीता छै कि की वू खाड़ी में काम करै लेली वापस आबी सकै छै ।

नेपाल बतौलनि जे, हुनका सभ केँ ई नहि बुझल छनि जे हुनका सभ केँ जेबाक अनुमति भेटतनि, वेतनभोगी छुट्टी भेटतनि वा, भले ओ सभ बिना वेतनक छुट्टी पर जेबाक लेल तैयार होथि, मुदा हुनका सभ केँ जेबाक अनुमति भेटतनि कि नहि।

अनुमति प्राप्त करय आ उड़ान के लागत के कवर करय सं परे मजदूर के आशंका छनि जे हुनकर आजीविका पर दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव पड़य.

"हुनका सब मे स बहुतो कए एहि काज क जरूरत अछि, खास क अगर आपदा मे हुनकर घर आ संपत्ति गंवा देल गेल अछि। हुनका इ जानबाक जरूरत अछि जे हुनका सब कए एखनो वापसी करबाक काज रहत।"

नेपाल वर्तमान चिन्ता के तुलना Covid-19 लॉकडाउन स करैत क्षेत्र के श्रम प्रायोजकता के ढाँचा एहि गतिहीनता के आओर बढ़ाबैत अछि, ई बतौलनि ।

हुनी नोट करलकै कि प्रवासी मजदूरऽ लेली हुनकऽ गतिशीलता के आजादी के मामला म॑ एक व्यवस्थित तरह के भयावहता छै, ई तरह के कठिन परिस्थिति म॑ भी कफला प्रणाली प्रासंगिक छै ।

ओ कहला जे हम सब 2020 मे सेहो एहने स्थिति देखलहुं... ओ सब सचमुच अपन परिवार मे वापस आबय चाहैत छलाह, मुदा हुनका सब कए इ करबा स रोकल गेल। ई एकदम अमानवीय प्रकारक स्थिति बुझाइत अछि।”

'शून्य सँ शुरू'।

कतार मे 37 वर्षीय ड्राइवर शिव उज्जवल ठीक वैह दुःस्वप्न जीबि रहल छथि।

उज्जवल न॑ पिछला तीन साल दोहा केरऽ बाहरी इलाका म॑ हजारों सफाईकर्मी आरू निर्माण मजदूरऽ क॑ रखै वाला श्रम शिविरऽ स॑ मजदूरऽ क॑ खाड़ी के राजधानी म॑ बिंदीदार कार्यालय आरू भवन स्थल प॑ पहुँचै म॑ बिताबै छै ।

ड्राइवर भोरे-भोर पाली शुरू क रहल छल कि आपदा आबि गेल। सोशल मीडिया चेक करबाक मौका नहि भेटला पर ओ पहिने संगी कार्यकर्ता स इ खबर सुनलथि।

जखन हुनकर सुपरवाइजर हुनका अपन फोन के उपयोग करय देलखिन्ह त हुनकर घर के उन्मादी कॉल फेल भ गेल छल - एहि क्षेत्र के संचार नेटवर्क पूरा तरह सं कट गेल छल.

उज्जवल कहलनि जे, पहिल बेर ऑनलाइन विनाशकारी वीडियो देखबाक स्मरण करैत उज्जवल कहलनि जे, हमर दिल टूटि रहल छल।

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला (पेड्रो पारदो/एएफपी) में आएल आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद 7 सितम्बर के काठमांडू में मुर्दाघर के बाहर फोटो देखैत एकटा महिला

“बाढ़िक पैमाना सँ हम सहजहि कल्पना क’ सकैत छलहुँ जे हमर घर छीन लेल गेल अछि, मुदा हम अपन परिवारक लेल बहुत चिंतित छलहुँ।”

जखन कि ओकर पत्नी, बच्चा आ माता-पिता सुरक्षित भागबा मे सफल रहलाह, मुदा चारूकातक मानवीय टोल डगमगाइत छल। ओकर नौ परिजन मारल गेलै, आ ओकर गामक अनगिनत लोक लापता अछि।

ओ बतौलनि जे हमर परिवारक लोक खाली हाथ दौड़ैत छल, कोनो महत्वपूर्ण कागज, पाइ, सोना लेबाक कोनो मौका नहि छल।

“लाइव गोली टाइप के बाढ़ि के एक बेर मारला स पांच सेकेंड स कम समय मे हम सब अपन सबटा संपत्ति गंवा देलहुं।”

पुनर्निर्माण के बोझ

तीन साल पहिने कतार जेबा स पहिने सऊदी अरब आ यूएई मे काज केनिहार उज्जवल लेल भौतिक नुकसान सालों स मेटाएल श्रम क प्रतिनिधित्व करैत अछि।

ओ अपन परिवार’क घर केँ कतेको साल मे चरणबद्ध तरीका सँ मेहनति सँ बनौने छलाह, अपन मामूली बचत’क उपयोग एक-एक मंजिल’क फंडिंग मे करैत छलाह. भले ही हुनकऽ खाड़ी केरऽ मजदूरी मामूली छेलै, लेकिन ई मौका “हुनकरऽ किचन क॑ रोशन” करै म॑ मदद करलकै आरू हुनकऽ परिवार क॑ तैरते रखै म॑ मदद करलकै । आब हुनका सामने शून्य स शुरूआत करबाक भयावह संभावना अछि।

‘लाइव गोली टाइप बाढ़िक एकहि प्रहारसँ पाँच सेकेण्डसँ कम समयमे हमर सभटा सम्पत्ति गमा लेलक’ - कतारमे नेपाली मजदूर शिवा उज्जवल

हुनकऽ सुपरवाइजर हुनका बिना वेतन के छुट्टी प॑ वापस नेपाल भेजै के व्यवस्था करी रहलऽ छै, लेकिन भौगोलिक आरू भावनात्मक दूरी के भारी असर पड़लऽ छै, खास करी क॑ प्रारंभिक बहुदिवसीय संचार ब्लैकआउट के दौरान ।

अंततः अपन घर के कोना फेर सं बनाओल जाय, एहि सोच सं बोझिल ओ कहलनि जे, एतय रहब बहुत तनावपूर्ण अछि, किया कि हमर परिवार आब होल्डिंग सेंटर मे अछि। “हमर देह एतय अछि, मुदा हम एतय नहि छी।”

खाड़ी मे नेपाली प्रवासी लेल तत्काल प्रतिक्रिया जुटान रहल अछि । जमीनी स्तर पर धन उगाही के अभियान व्हाट्सएप ग्रुप के माध्यम सं चलि रहल अछि, कियाकि मजदूर अपन मामूली बचत के एकत्रित क क सबस बेसी प्रभावित जिला मे थोक राहत भेजैत छथि।

तइयो उज्ज्वल आ कृष्ण सन पुरुष लेल आर्थिक सहयोग घर रहबाक खोखला विकल्प जकाँ बुझाइत अछि ।

title: S. Korea to send 2nd disaster relief team to Nepal over floods - Yonhap News Agency
description: S. Korea to send 2nd disaster relief team to Nepal over floods  Yonhap News Agency
publisher.title: Yonhap News Agency
full_article:
SEOUL, Sept. 10 (Yonhap) -- South Korea's second overseas emergency relief team will be sent to Nepal this week to support recovery efforts following devastating floods and landslides, the foreign ministry said Thursday.

The eight-member Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) will depart aboard a KC-330 military transport aircraft and arrive in Nepal on Friday, consisting of officials from the ministry, firefighters, Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) personnel and medical staff, according to the ministry.

The team, which also includes a small number of rescue personnel, will focus mainly on reconstruction and recovery operations during its seven-day mission, it added.

The first 44-member contingent of the KDRT, which was dispatched to Nepal last week, will return home after wrapping up its 10-day search-and-rescue mission.

Nine Koreans -- six employees of Doosan Enerbility Co. and three of Korea South-East Power Co. -- went missing Aug. 26 after massive floods and landslides hit Rasuwa District near the Nepal-Tibet border while they were working at a hydropower plant construction site.

The KDRT, in cooperation with local authorities and corporate response teams, has conducted intensive searches using drones, helicopters and other advanced equipment, but no signs of the missing people have been found.



Members of the Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) prepare to conduct a drone search in the area around the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower plant and powerhouse in Rasuwa District, Nepal, on Sept. 8, 2026, in this photo provided by the KDRT. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

Family members of South Korean nationals missing after massive floods and landslides in Nepal wipe away tears during a press conference at a hotel in Kathmandu on Sept. 9, 2026. (Yonhap)

title: Nepal-Tibet Floods: Questions Over China's Impact on Tibetan Plateau - japan-forward.com
description: Nepal-Tibet Floods: Questions Over China's Impact on Tibetan Plateau  japan-forward.com
publisher.title: japan-forward.com
full_article:
The recent Tibet-Nepal massive flash flood on 26 August claimed thousands of lives. It caused catastrophic damage to property and infrastructure along Tibet's Kyidrong Valley, Nepal's Rasuwa District, and downstream settlements.

Pictures and videos showing the devastating force of the glacial torrent as it inundated and engulfed everything in its way are a clear warning that the Tibetan Plateau—known as the "Water Tower of Asia" and the "Third Pole of the Earth"—is not safe in the hands of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)'s regime.

As of now, based on media reports from Nepal, at least 1,287 people, including foreigners, have been killed, and more than 5,000 are missing. Full efforts are being made to expand relief work with the support of the international community.

On the Tibet side of the border, however, information from China has been limited from the start. It initially reported three dead and 558 missing; now it is 43 dead and 519 missing.

International Campaign for Tibet Director Tenchoe Gyatso has rightly said, "What is visible in Nepal exposes what is being concealed in Tibet."

A global press watchdog has condemned China's information blackout of Tibet during the devastating flash flood crisis. Beijing barred international media from entering the region for around ten days after the disaster, for fear that the real situation and cause of the devastating flood would be revealed.

The CCP is more interested in saving its image. That is why we see many videos and pictures showing Chinese rescue teams in full professional gear and helicopters hovering, but with no information on what they are actually doing.

Beijing has also reported that the disaster originated on the Nepal side.

Tibet's Ecological Importance

Since ancient times, Tibetans have preserved and worshiped the mountains, rivers, and forests. This has greatly helped maintain the required ecological balance, allowing the glaciers, lakes, and rivers to stay in harmony with the people.

Tibet is the source of some ten major rivers that nourish more than 2 billion people downstream. The Indus, Sutlej, Ganges, and Brahmaputra are major rivers and tributaries flowing to India, Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

In the east, the Huang He and Yangtze rivers of China; the Mekong River that flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam; and the Salween River that flows through China, Myanmar, and Thailand originate on the Tibetan Plateau.

A Zone of Peace

H.H. the Dalai Lama proposed in 1987 that Tibet be a zone of peace, a fully demilitarized autonomous state, to serve as a peaceful buffer state and another Geneva to discuss world peace and resolve international differences.

This would have greatly helped avert many of the violent clashes and man-made natural disasters that we saw along the borders that Tibet shares with Nepal, India, and Bhutan.

H.H. Dalai Lama praying (Gaden Phodrang file photo) THJ

For centuries, the riparian nations in the south enjoyed a steady flow of fresh river waters from Tibet and peaceful coexistence and exchange along the borders. This was what H.H. the Dalai Lama dreamt of reviving for peace in the regions and for the world.

But the modern world, in the name of national interest, acquiesced to the fiery red dragon's whim, and what we are seeing is the result of the dragon's noxious and deadly hegemonic fumes.

Militarization and Environmental Damage

Contrary to what the Dalai Lama proposed, China has militarized the Tibetan Plateau and exploited its natural resources through extensive mining, deforestation, and damming.

To further fortify its claim on Tibet, the regime has built more than 650 dual-purpose settlements, housing military personnel and forcibly displaced nomads, along the southern borders with Nepal, India, and Bhutan.

Growing International Concerns

Tibetans and environment scientists have warned that the increased military, mining, damming, and infrastructural buildings could trigger ecological disaster in the region, affecting the lives of millions of people of the downstream nations.

Many have raised this question at the annual UN Climate Change Conference, but the CCP regime, bent on its hegemonic ambition to exploit and control the Himalayan region, has continued to ravage the Tibetan plateau.

Brahma Chellanney, an Indian geo-strategist and author of Water: Asia's New Battleground , has said that the Tibet-Nepal flood disaster is a stark reminder that humanity must stop trying to bend nature to its will.

Penpa Tsering, Prime Minister of the Central Tibetan Administration, warned in a recent talk in Delhi about the potential environmental consequences of China's large-scale dam and infrastructure projects in Tibet for downstream countries.

Tibetan Prime Minister (Sikyong) Penpa Tsering addressing the public on September 2 at Dharamsala. (Tibet.net)

Separately, Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that questions about why the ice and rock collapsed and how such a large volume of water was generated must be answered by the global community.

Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has rightly stressed that as China, India, and Nepal face similar environmental challenges and share the same ecosystem, they should take collective responsibility for addressing climate change in the Himalayas.

Furthermore, a senior UN official has warned that the Himalayan region faces severe risks from future glacial floods.

Beijing's Narrative

The CCP regime's mouthpiece, Global Times, has said that glacier disasters could become more frequent as global warming further weakens glacier stability on the Tibetan Plateau, in an apparent attempt to suggest that China has had no hand in the recent disaster.

To pass off the devastating disaster as a usual natural disaster, Gao Rong, Deputy Director of the China Meteorological Administration, is reported to have said that global warming is accelerating the melting of mountain glaciers worldwide.

Just as in the January 2025 earthquake in Tibet, instead of finding the real cause of the disaster, Beijing is suppressing information and trying to control the narratives. It is shying away from responsibility by attributing the disaster to global warming, but the question here is what induced the warming in the region.

A major factor is the increased militarization, mining, damming, and infrastructural construction on the Tibetan Plateau by the CCP regime.

This time, it was not only a glacial collapse, but a collapse of the rock beneath, a clear indication that the constant damming and mining have weakened the stability of the mountains' bedrock, giving way to the pressure of the glacier.

Holding China Accountable

It is reported that Beijing is mulling a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028 (COP33). This is a great relief and, at the same time, alarming.

It is a relief because hosting the talks could provide an opportunity to hold Beijing accountable, but alarming because it may misuse the forum to justify its wrongdoings on the Tibetan Plateau.

This is exactly what China did with the 2008 Olympic bid, and the world supported it with the hope that the Olympics would help integrate China into international democratic norms and values—but what we see right now is exactly the opposite.

This flood disaster is a strong warning not only to Nepal, India, Bhutan, and Bangladesh, but also to all the Mekong nations of Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Burma.

If the CCP regime keeps militarizing the Tibetan Plateau and its border, mining minerals, cutting trees, and damming the rivers, such disasters are bound to occur from time to time. These disasters are not mere natural calamities, but Chinese-made disasters.

Instead of conducting relief work and helping displaced people, China is arresting and punishing people for posting and sharing information about the flood on social networks. It even condemned the Spanish football club Real Madrid for observing a moment of silence in memory of the victims of the devastating flood.

Tibetans and Japanese offering prayer service at Tibet House Japan on September 5.

Tibetans and Japanese gathered on September 5 for a prayer service for those who lost their lives and were affected by the disaster at Tibet House in Tokyo.

Many voiced that China should be held responsible for this man-made disaster because of its rampant colonial-style hegemonic activities on the Tibetan Plateau. Many also felt indignant that China did not warn Nepal despite having enough time to do so.

H.H. the Dalai Lama, while praying for the victims of the flood and the early recovery of the situation, reminded us that we all have a responsibility to take appropriate follow-up measures to ensure that such disasters do not recur.

The international community needs to ensure that those affected in Nepal and Tibet are adequately rehabilitated, and Beijing must be held accountable for this devastating disaster and warned not to further damage the ecology of Tibet.

This flood disaster should be one of the core issues during the upcoming 2026 United Nation Climate Change Conference (COP31) this November in Turkey.

Author: Tsewang Gyalpo Arya

Dr Tsewang Gyalpo Arya is the former Secretary of the Department of Information and International Relations and former Director of the Tibet Policy Institute. He is currently the Representative of the Liaison Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama for Japan and East Asia. His books include Harnessing the Dragon's Fume and The Ancient Tibetan Civilization. The views expressed above are the author's own.

हालहि मे 26 अगस्त कए तिब्बत-नेपाल मे आयल विशाल आकस्मिक बाढ़ि मे हजारों लोकक जान गेल छल। एहि सँ तिब्बतक कीद्रोंग घाटी, नेपालक रसुवा जिला, आ नीचाँक बस्तीक कात मे संपत्ति आ बुनियादी ढांचा केँ भयावह क्षति पहुँचल ।

हिमनदीय धार केरऽ विनाशकारी ताकत क॑ देखाबै वाला तस्वीर आरू वीडियो जेकरा म॑ ई अपनऽ रास्ता म॑ सब कुछ क॑ बाढ़ म॑ डूबी क॑ घेर लेलकै, ई बात के स्पष्ट चेतावनी छै कि तिब्बती पठार – जेकरा क॑ “एशिया केरऽ वाटर टावर” आरू “पृथ्वी केरऽ तीसरा ध्रुव” के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै – चीनी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी (सीसीपी) केरऽ शासन के हाथऽ म॑ सुरक्षित नै छै ।

एखन धरि नेपाल सं आयल मीडिया रिपोर्ट के आधार पर विदेशी सहित कम सं कम 1287 लोक के मौत भ चुकल अछि, आओर 5000 सं बेसि लोक लापता अछि. अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय के सहयोग स॑ राहत कार्य के विस्तार के पूरा प्रयास करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

सीमा केरऽ तिब्बत तरफ, हालांकि चीन स॑ मिललऽ जानकारी शुरू स॑ ही सीमित रहलऽ छै । शुरू मे एहि मे तीन गोटेक मौत आ 558 गोटे लापता हेबाक सूचना भेटल छल; आब एकर मृत्यु 43 आ 519 लापता अछि।

तिब्बत के लेलऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अभियान के निदेशक तेन्चो ग्यात्सो न॑ सही तरीका स॑ कहल॑ छै कि नेपाल म॑ जे कुछ दिखाई दै छै, वू तिब्बत म॑ जे छिपलऽ छै ओकरा उजागर करै छै ।

वैश्विक प्रेस वॉचडॉग न॑ चीन केरऽ विनाशकारी फ्लैश फ्लड संकट के दौरान तिब्बत केरऽ सूचना ब्लैकआउट के निंदा करलकै । बीजिंग न॑ आपदा के बाद लगभग दस दिन तलक अंतरराष्ट्रीय मीडिया क॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ प्रवेश करै स॑ रोकी देलकै, ई डर स॑ कि ई विनाशकारी बाढ़ केरऽ वास्तविक स्थिति आरू कारण के खुलासा होय जैतै ।

सीसीपी कए अपन छवि कए बचाबय मे बेसी रुचि अछि। यही लेली हमरा सब क॑ बहुत सारा वीडियो आरू तस्वीर देखै ल॑ मिलै छै जेकरा म॑ चीनी बचाव टीम क॑ पूरा प्रोफेशनल गियर म॑ आरू हेलीकॉप्टर मंडराबै वाला देखाबै छै, लेकिन ओकरा वास्तव म॑ की करी रहलऽ छै, एकरऽ कोय जानकारी नै छै ।

बीजिंग सेहो नेपाल दिस सँ ई आपदा उत्पन्न भेल अछि ।

तिब्बत के पारिस्थितिक महत्व

प्राचीन काल सँ तिब्बती लोकनि पहाड़, नदी, आ जंगलक संरक्षण आ पूजा करैत आबि रहल छथि | एकरा स॑ आवश्यक पारिस्थितिकी संतुलन बनाबै म॑ बहुत मदद मिललऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ ग्लेशियर, झील, आरू नदी लोगऽ के साथ सामंजस्य बनलऽ रहै छै ।

तिब्बत लगभग दस प्रमुख नदी के स्रोत छै जे 2 अरब स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ क॑ नीचें के पोषण करै छै । सिन्धु, सतलज, गंडक, आ ब्रह्मपुत्र भारत, नेपाल, भूटान, पाकिस्तान, आ बांग्लादेश मे बहय बला प्रमुख नदी आ सहायक नदी छी ।

पूर्व में चीनक हुआंग हे आ यांग्त्ज़ी नदी ; मेकांग नदी जे चीन, म्यांमार, लाओस, थाईलैंड, कम्बोडिया, आ वियतनाम सं होइत अछि ; आरू चीन, म्यांमार, आरू थाईलैंड स॑ गुजरै वाला सलवीन नदी के उत्पत्ति तिब्बती पठार स॑ होय छै ।

शांति के एक क्षेत्र

एच.एच.दलाई लामा न॑ १९८७ म॑ प्रस्ताव रखलकै कि तिब्बत शांति केरऽ क्षेत्र, पूर्ण रूप स॑ निसैन्य स्वायत्त राज्य, शांतिपूर्ण बफर राज्य के रूप म॑ काम करै आरू विश्व शांति प॑ चर्चा आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मतभेद के समाधान लेली एगो आरू जिनेवा होय ।

एहि सं बहुत रास हिंसक झड़प आ मानव निर्मित प्राकृतिक आपदा जे हम सब सीमा पर देखलहुं जे तिब्बत नेपाल, भारत, आ भूटान सं साझा अछि, ओकरा टालबा में बहुत मददगार होइत.

एच.एच.दलाई लामा प्रार्थना करते हुए (गडेन फोडरंग फाइल फोटो) THJ

सदियो स॑ दक्षिण केरऽ तटीय राष्ट्रऽ म॑ तिब्बत स॑ नदी केरऽ ताजा पानी केरऽ लगातार प्रवाह आरू सीमा के साथ शांतिपूर्ण सह-अस्तित्व आरू आदान-प्रदान के आनंद मिललै । इएह छल जे प.ह.दलाई लामा क्षेत्र मे शांति आ दुनिया लेल पुनर्जीवित करबाक सपना देखने छलाह ।

लेकिन आधुनिक दुनिया, राष्ट्रीय हित के नाम पर, उग्र लाल अजगर के सनक के सहमति देलकै, आरू जे देखै छियै, वू अजगर के हानिकारक आरू घातक वर्चस्ववादी धुँआ के परिणाम छै.

सैन्यीकरण एवं पर्यावरण क्षति

दलाई लामा केरऽ प्रस्ताव के विपरीत चीन न॑ तिब्बती पठार क॑ सैन्यीकरण करी क॑ व्यापक खनन, जंगलऽ के कटाई आरू बांध के माध्यम स॑ ओकरऽ प्राकृतिक संसाधनऽ के दोहन करलकै ।

तिब्बत पर अपनऽ दावा क॑ आरू मजबूत करै लेली शासन न॑ नेपाल, भारत आरू भूटान के साथ दक्षिणी सीमा के साथ ६५० स॑ भी अधिक द्विउद्देशीय बस्ती के निर्माण करलकै, जेकरा म॑ सैन्य कर्मी आरू जबरन विस्थापित खानाबदोश लोगऽ के आवास छै ।

बढ़ते अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सरोकार

तिब्बती आरू पर्यावरण वैज्ञानिक न॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै कि बढ़लऽ सैन्य, खनन, बांध, आरू बुनियादी ढांचागत भवनऽ स॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ पारिस्थितिकी आपदा पैदा होय सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ नीचे के राष्ट्रऽ के लाखों लोगऽ के जीवन प्रभावित होय सकै छै ।

बहुतो न॑ ई सवाल संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ वार्षिक जलवायु परिवर्तन सम्मेलन म॑ उठैल॑ छै, लेकिन हिमालयी क्षेत्र केरऽ शोषण आरू नियंत्रण केरऽ अपनऽ वर्चस्ववादी महत्वाकांक्षा प॑ झुकलऽ सीसीपी शासन न॑ तिब्बती पठार प॑ तबाही मचाबै के काम जारी रखन॑ छै ।

भारतीय भू-रणनीतिज्ञ आरू जल: एशिया केरऽ नया युद्धक्षेत्र केरऽ लेखक ब्रह्मा चेलानी न॑ कहल॑ छै कि तिब्बत-नेपाल बाढ़ केरऽ आपदा एगो सख्त याद दिलाबै वाला छै कि मानवता क॑ प्रकृति क॑ अपनऽ मर्जी के हिसाब स॑ मोड़ै के कोशिश करना बंद करना चाहियऽ ।

मध्य तिब्बती प्रशासन केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री पेनपा त्सेरिंग न॑ हाल ही म॑ दिल्ली म॑ एगो बातचीत म॑ चीन केरऽ तिब्बत म॑ बड़ऽ पैमाना प॑ बांध आरू बुनियादी ढांचागत परियोजना केरऽ डाउनस्ट्रीम देशऽ लेली संभावित पर्यावरणीय परिणाम के बारे म॑ चेतावनी देलकै ।

तिब्बती प्रधानमंत्री (सिक्योंग) पेनपा त्सेरिंग 2 सितम्बर कए धर्मशाला मे जनता कए संबोधित करैत। (तिब्बत डॉट नेट) २.

अलग-अलग नेपालक प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह कहलनि जे, बर्फ आ चट्टान किएक खसल आ एतेक पैघ मात्रा मे पानि कोना उत्पन्न भेल ताहि पर प्रश्नक उत्तर वैश्विक समुदाय केँ देबय पड़त।

नेपाल केरऽ विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल न॑ सही तरीका स॑ जोर देल॑ छै कि चीन, भारत, आरू नेपाल क॑ समान पर्यावरणीय चुनौती के सामना करना पड़ै छै आरू एक ही पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र के साझा छै, ई लेली हिमालय म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ निपटै के सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी लेन॑ चाहियऽ ।

एकरऽ अलावा संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एगो वरिष्ठ अधिकारी न॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै कि हिमालय क्षेत्र क॑ भविष्य म॑ हिमनदीय बाढ़ स॑ गंभीर खतरा के सामना करना पड़॑ छै ।

बीजिंग के कथ्य

सीसीपी शासन केरऽ मुखपत्र ग्लोबल टाइम्स न॑ कहल॑ छै कि ग्लेशियर आपदा आरू बार बढ़ी सकै छै, कैन्हेंकि ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के वजह स॑ तिब्बती पठार प॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ स्थिरता आरू कमजोर होय जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ ई बात के स्पष्ट कोशिश छै कि चीन केरऽ हाल केरऽ आपदा म॑ कोनो हाथ नै रहलऽ छै ।

खबर छै कि चीन मौसम प्रशासन केरऽ उपनिदेशक गाओ रोंग न॑ ई विनाशकारी आपदा क॑ सामान्य प्राकृतिक आपदा के रूप म॑ पेश करै लेली कहल॑ छै कि ग्लोबल वार्मिंग स॑ दुनिया भर म॑ पहाड़ी ग्लेशियर केरऽ पिघलना म॑ तेजी आबी रहलऽ छै ।

जेना जनवरी २०२५ म॑ तिब्बत म॑ आयलऽ भूकंप म॑ बीजिंग आपदा केरऽ असली कारण खोजै के बजाय सूचना क॑ दबाबै छै आरू कथ्य क॑ नियंत्रित करै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छै । ई आपदा क॑ ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के कारण बताय क॑ जिम्मेदारी स॑ परहेज करी रहलऽ छै, लेकिन यहाँ सवाल ई छै कि ई क्षेत्र म॑ वार्मिंग क॑ की प्रेरित करलकै ।

एकरऽ एगो प्रमुख कारक छै सीसीपी शासन द्वारा तिब्बती पठार प॑ बढ़लऽ सैन्यीकरण, खनन, बांध, आरू बुनियादी ढांचागत निर्माण ।

एहि बेर ई मात्र हिमनदीक ढहब नहिं, नीचाक चट्टानक ढहब छल, जे एकर स्पष्ट संकेत छल जे लगातार बांध आ खनन सं पहाड़क बेडरोकक स्थिरता कमजोर भ गेल अछि, जाहि सं ग्लेशियरक दबाव कें जगह भेटि गेल अछि.

चीन के जवाबदेह बनाना

खबर छै कि बीजिंग २०२८ (COP33) म॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु वार्ता के मेजबानी करै के बोली प॑ विचार करी रहलऽ छै । ई बहुत राहत के बात छै आरू साथ ही साथ चिंताजनक भी छै ।

ई राहत के बात छै, कैन्हेंकि वार्ता के मेजबानी करला स॑ बीजिंग क॑ जवाबदेह ठहराबै के मौका मिल॑ सकै छै, लेकिन चिंताजनक छै, कैन्हेंकि ई मंच केरऽ दुरुपयोग करी क॑ तिब्बती पठार प॑ अपनऽ गलत काम क॑ जायज ठहराबै सकै छै ।

2008 केरऽ ओलंपिक बोली के साथ चीन न॑ ठीक वैसनऽ ही करलकै, आरू दुनिया न॑ एकरऽ समर्थन ई आशा स॑ करलकै कि ओलंपिक चीन क॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय लोकतांत्रिक मानदंड आरू मूल्यऽ म॑ शामिल करै म॑ मदद करतै-लेकिन अभी जे देखै छियै, वू एकरऽ ठीक उल्टा छै ।

ई बाढ़िक आपदा नेपाल, भारत, भूटान, आरू बांग्लादेश लेली ही नै, बल्कि लाओस, कम्बोडिया, वियतनाम, थाईलैंड, आरू बर्मा केरऽ सब मेकांग राष्ट्र लेली भी एगो कड़ा चेतावनी छै ।

अगर सीसीपी शासन तिब्बती पठार आरू ओकरऽ सीमा क॑ सैन्यीकरण करतें रहतै, खनिज के खनन करतें रहतै, गाछ काटतें रहतै, आरू नदी क॑ बांध बनाबैत॑ रहतै त॑ समय-समय प॑ ऐसनऽ आपदा होना तय छै । ई आपदा सब खाली प्राकृतिक आपदा नै छै, बल्कि चीनी निर्मित आपदा छै ।

चीन राहत कार्य करै आरू विस्थापित लोगऽ के मदद करै के बजाय सोशल नेटवर्क प॑ बाढ़ के बारे म॑ जानकारी पोस्ट करी क॑ साझा करै वाला लोगऽ क॑ गिरफ्तार करी क॑ सजा द॑ रहलऽ छै । त॑ स्पेनिश फुटबॉल क्लब रियल मैड्रिड केरऽ निंदा तक करलकै कि हुनी विनाशकारी बाढ़ के शिकार लोगऽ के याद म॑ एक पल के मौन रखलकै ।

5 सितंबर कए तिब्बती हाउस जापान मे प्रार्थना सेवा दैत तिब्बती आ जापानी।

टोक्यो केरऽ तिब्बत हाउस म॑ अपनऽ जान गंवाय देलऽ गेलऽ आरू आपदा स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ लेली प्रार्थना सेवा लेली ५ सितंबर क॑ तिब्बती आरू जापानी जमा होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

बहुतो लोगऽ न॑ आवाज उठैलकै कि चीन क॑ ई मानव निर्मित आपदा लेली जिम्मेदार ठहराबै के चाही, कैन्हेंकि तिब्बती पठार प॑ ओकरऽ बेतहाशा औपनिवेशिक शैली केरऽ वर्चस्ववादी गतिविधि छै । बहुतो गोटे के ईहो आक्रोश भेल जे चीन नेपाल के चेताबय लेल पर्याप्त समय रहला के बादो नहि देलक।

प.पू.दलाई लामा, बाढ़ि के पीड़ित आ स्थिति के जल्दी ठीक होय के प्रार्थना करैत हमरा सब के याद दिला देलखिन जे हमरा सब के जिम्मेदारी अछि जे एहि तरहक आपदा के दोबारा नहि आबय लेल उचित अनुवर्ती उपाय करी।

अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय क॑ ई सुनिश्चित करै के जरूरत छै कि नेपाल आरू तिब्बत म॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ क॑ पर्याप्त रूप स॑ पुनर्वास करलऽ जाय, आरू बीजिंग क॑ ई विनाशकारी आपदा लेली जवाबदेह ठहराबै के जरूरत छै आरू चेतावनी देना चाहियऽ कि तिब्बत केरऽ पारिस्थितिकी क॑ आरू नुकसान नै पहुँचै ।

ई बाढ़ आपदा क॑ ई नवंबर म॑ तुर्की म॑ होबै वाला २०२६ संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु परिवर्तन सम्मेलन (सीओपी३१) के दौरान मुख्य मुद्दा म॑ स॑ एक होना चाहियऽ ।

लेखक: त्सेवांग ग्याल्पो आर्य

डॉ. त्सेवांग ग्याल्पो आर्य सूचना आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संबंध विभाग केरऽ पूर्व सचिव आरू तिब्बत नीति संस्थान केरऽ पूर्व निदेशक छै । वर्तमान में जापान आरू पूर्वी एशिया के लेलऽ परम पूज्य दलाई लामा के संपर्क कार्यालय के प्रतिनिधि छै । हुनकऽ किताबऽ म॑ हार्नेसिंग द ड्रैगन केरऽ धुआँ आरू द एन्शियंट तिब्बती सिविलाइजेशन शामिल छै । ऊपर जे विचार व्यक्त कयल गेल अछि से लेखकक अपन अछि ।

full_article:
ELEPHANTS IN THE FOG announces itself first through sound. The screen remains dark. What arrives is chanting from villagers patrolling the edge of their settlement, a collective rhythm to guard against fear. “It is a collective scream transformed into a vocal rhythm, used to maintain their composure,” the director, Abinash Bikram Shah, told me. “They are all deeply terrified, and it is through this shared screaming that they summon their courage.” The chant is built from a traditional Nepali bhajan , or devotional song, its words arranged to turn a cry of fear into “a shield of sound”. This opening composition sets the tone for the composer Frédéric Alvarez’s score throughout the film, which returns again and again to the line between human voice and instrument, rarely letting either dominate.

The cinematographer, Noé Bach, captures the forested village in Thori, in the Terai plains of southern Nepal, in its quietest register: fog-laden winter afternoons and evenings, the light flat and grey, the jungle never quite letting the eye settle. It is a landscape shot less for spectacle than for atmosphere, the fog doing as much narrative work as any line of dialogue.

Slowly, shapes emerge. Villagers with torches and flares try to scare away elephants entering from the forest, the same animal they worship. Across Nepal, as well as much of India and Southasia, the elephant represents the deity Ganesha, remover of obstacles and patron of the arts and sciences, his idols and images present in almost every Hindu home. In the Terai, this same animal is jolted by electrified fences, driven away and sometimes killed by people desperate to protect their fields and homes from its intrusions. Shah lingers on one striking image: massive red eyes painted onto tree trunks at the forest’s edge, another of the measures the villagers deploy to try and repel the elephants.

ELEPHANTS IN THE FOG ध्वनि के माध्यम स पहिने अपन घोषणा करैत अछि। पर्दा अन्हार रहैत अछि। जे पहुँचै छै, वू छै अपनऽ बस्ती के किनारे गश्त करी रहलऽ ग्रामीणऽ के नारा, जे भय स॑ बचाव लेली एगो सामूहिक लय छै । निर्देशक अबीनाश बिक्रम शाह हमरा कहलनि जे, ई एकटा सामूहिक चीत्कार अछि जे स्वर लय मे बदलि गेल अछि, जकर उपयोग हुनकर संयम के कायम रखबाक लेल कयल जाइत अछि। “सब गहींर आतंकित छै, आरू ई साझा चिल्लाहट के माध्यम स॑ ही वू अपनऽ हिम्मत के आह्वान करै छै।” ई जाप पारंपरिक नेपाली भजन , या भक्ति गीत स बनल अछि, एकर शब्द भय के एकटा क्रन्दन के “ध्वनि के ढाल” में बदलय के व्यवस्था कयल गेल अछि | ई उद्घाटन रचना पूरा फिल्म में संगीतकार फ्रेडरिक अल्वारेज़ के स्कोर के टोन सेट करै छै, जे बार-बार मानव आवाज आरू वाद्ययंत्र के बीच के रेखा पर वापस आबै छै, जेकरा स॑ शायद ही कभी दोनों में स॑ कोय भी हावी होय जाय छै ।

सिनेमाटोग्राफर नोए बाख दक्षिणी नेपालक तराई मैदानमें थोरीक जंगली गामकें अपन सब सं शांत रजिस्टरमें कैद केने छथि : कोहरा सं भरल जाड़क दुपहर आ साँझ, हल्का समतल आ धूसर रंग, जंगल कहियो एकदम सं आँखि कें बसय नहिं दैत अछि. ई वातावरण स बेसी तमाशा लेल कम शूट कएल गेल लैंडस्केप अछि, कोहरा ओतबे कथ्यक काज करैत अछि जतेक कोनो संवादक लाइन ।

धीरे-धीरे आकृति सभ उभरैत अछि। मशाल आ फ्लेयर ल क ग्रामीण जंगल स प्रवेश करय वाला हाथी के डराबै के कोशिश करैत छैथ, जे जानवर के ओ सब पूजा करैत छैथ। पूरा नेपाल के साथ-साथ भारत आरू दक्षिण एशिया के बहुत हिस्सा में हाथी गणेश देवता के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै, जे बाधा दूर करै वाला आरू कला आरू विज्ञान के संरक्षक छै, ओकरऽ मूर्ति आरू प्रतिमा लगभग हर हिन्दू घर में मौजूद छै । तराई में ई वही जानवर के बिजली के बाड़ से झटका देलऽ जाय छै, भगा देलऽ जाय छै आरू कखनी-कखनी ओकरऽ घुसपैठ स॑ अपनऽ खेत आरू घर के बचाबै लेली बेताब लोगऽ द्वारा मारलऽ जाय छै । शाह एकटा हड़ताली छवि पर टिकल रहैत छथि : जंगलक कात मे गाछक तने पर रंगल विशाल लाल आँखि, एकटा आओर उपाय जे गामक लोक हाथी केँ भगाब’ के कोशिश मे लगाबैत छथि.

title: (LEAD) S. Korea to send 2nd disaster relief team to Nepal as flood response shifts to recovery - Yonhap News Agency
description: (LEAD) S. Korea to send 2nd disaster relief team to Nepal as flood response shifts to recovery  Yonhap News Agency
publisher.title: Yonhap News Agency
full_article:

SEOUL, Sept. 10 (Yonhap) -- South Korea will send its second overseas emergency relief team to Nepal this week to support the country's shift of its focus from search and rescue to recovery following devastating floods, Seoul's foreign ministry said Thursday.

The eight-member Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) will depart aboard a KC-330 military transport aircraft and arrive in Nepal on Friday, consisting of officials from the ministry, firefighters, Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) personnel and medical staff, according to the ministry.

The team, which also includes a small number of rescue personnel, will focus mainly on reconstruction and recovery operations during its seven-day mission, it added.

Nine Koreans -- six employees of Doosan Enerbility Co. and three of Korea South-East Power Co. -- went missing Aug. 26 after massive floods and landslides hit Rasuwa District near the Nepal-Tibet border while they were working at a hydropower plant construction site.



Members of the Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) prepare to conduct a drone search in the area around the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower plant and powerhouse in Rasuwa District, Nepal, on Sept. 8, 2026, in this photo provided by the KDRT. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

"Nepal has decided to shift its operations from search and rescue to reconstruction and recovery and has asked us to support recovery efforts in the affected areas," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon said at a press briefing.

The first 44-member contingent of the KDRT, which was dispatched to Nepal last week, will return home after wrapping up its 10-day search-and-rescue mission.

The KDRT, in cooperation with local authorities and corporate response teams, has conducted intensive searches using drones, helicopters and other advanced equipment, but no signs of the missing people have been found.

Families of three missing Korea South-East Power employees opposed the planned conclusion of the first KDRT team's mission, urging authorities to continue ground searches in areas where they believe the workers may have evacuated.

President Lee Jae Myung has instructed officials to listen carefully to the families' opinions and review necessary measures to reflect their wishes as much as possible, according to the presidential office.

"The government understands how anxious and frustrated the families must be. We will listen to their concerns and review measures to respect and reflect their wishes," Park added.



Family members of South Korean nationals missing after massive floods and landslides in Nepal wipe away tears during a press conference at a hotel in Kathmandu on Sept. 9, 2026. (Yonhap)

कोरिया साउथ-ईस्ट पावर केरऽ तीन लापता कर्मचारी केरऽ परिवार न॑ पहलऽ केडीआरटी टीम केरऽ मिशन केरऽ योजनाबद्ध समापन के विरोध करतें हुअ॑ अधिकारियऽ स॑ आग्रह करलकै कि वू ऐन्हऽ इलाका म॑ जमीनी तलाशी जारी रख॑, जहां ओकरा लगै छै कि मजदूर खाली होय गेलऽ होतै ।

राष्ट्रपति कार्यालय के अनुसार राष्ट्रपति ली जे म्यूंग न॑ अधिकारियऽ क॑ परिवारऽ के राय क॑ ध्यान स॑ सुनै आरू ओकरऽ इच्छा क॑ यथासंभव प्रतिबिंबित करै लेली आवश्यक उपायऽ के समीक्षा करै के निर्देश देल॑ छै ।

title: China provides climate forecasts to support Nepal's post-mudslide relief - chinadailyasia.com
description: China provides climate forecasts to support Nepal's post-mudslide relief  chinadailyasia.com
publisher.title: chinadailyasia.com
full_article:
In this file photo dated July 26, 2025, the MAZU system is on display at China Meteorological Administration's booth during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai. (PHOTO/XINHUA)

BEIJING - China's National Climate Center has been providing Nepal with rolling climate monitoring and forecast products to support rescue and relief efforts following a severe mudslide at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing, the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) said on Thursday.

Following the disaster, the center activated an emergency response and began providing climate services through a Nepal-customized cloud version of MAZU, China's homegrown artificial intelligence (AI)-powered meteorological early warning system.

It has also produced regular analyses of climate conditions in and around the disaster-hit area, along with extended-range forecasts looking several weeks ahead.

Under the CMA's coordination, the National Climate Center is providing Nepal with two main categories of products -- climate monitoring and climate forecasting.

For climate monitoring, the center produces five types of routine products covering conditions such as temperature, precipitation and soil drought. It also tracks 10 major climate indicators, including the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, or ENSO, and the Madden-Julian Oscillation, or MJO.

ENSO refers to a natural climate cycle that affects weather around the world. It includes the warm El Nino phase and the cold La Nina phase. Unlike ENSO, which is stationary, the MJO is an eastward-moving disturbance of clouds, rainfall, winds, and pressure that traverses the tropics and returns to its starting point in 30 to 60 days, on average.

ALSO READ: China steps up satellite-based meteorological support for Nepal

For climate prediction, the center is using Fengshun, an AI climate forecasting model, to provide Nepal with daily temperature and precipitation forecasts for up to 60 days, as well as outlooks for climate phenomena including ENSO and the MJO.

The National Climate Center is also working with the Third Pole Regional Climate Center Network. Since Aug 28, it has been supplying Nepal with rolling climate outlooks for the coming 15 to 30 days in response to the country's needs, providing additional meteorological information for post-disaster rescue and relief work.

The meteorological support is part of broader China-Nepal cooperation following the Aug 26 disaster, which was triggered by a fractured glacier on Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal at an elevation of around 5,200 meters. The glacier collapse generated an ice-rock avalanche that plunged rapidly to around 4,000 meters, scouring mountain slopes and developing into a massive debris flow.

The two sides held video weather consultations immediately after the event, according to the CMA. The administration has been providing Nepal with a range of meteorological products through MAZU, including multi-source satellite data and products from the Fengyun 3 and Fengyun 4 meteorological satellite series.

READ MORE: Police: Nepal mudslide death toll reaches 1,344

MAZU, which literally means "Sea Goddess" in China's Minnan culture, is the world's first national-level action plan in response to the United Nations' Early Warnings for All initiative. Since 2024, meteorological agencies in more than 40 countries have accessed MAZU through the cloud.

बीजिंग : चीन के राष्ट्रीय जलवायु केन्द्र नेपाल क॑ रोलिंग जलवायु निगरानी आरू पूर्वानुमान उत्पाद उपलब्ध कराबै के काम करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ ग्यारोंग-रासुवा सीमा पार प॑ भयंकर कीचड़ गिरला के बाद बचाव आरू राहत प्रयास के सहायता मिलै छै ।

आपदा के बाद केंद्र न॑ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया क॑ सक्रिय करी क॑ चीन केरऽ घरऽ म॑ बनलऽ आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (एआई) संचालित मौसम संबंधी पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली माजु केरऽ नेपाल द्वारा अनुकूलित क्लाउड संस्करण के माध्यम स॑ जलवायु सेवा प्रदान करना शुरू करलकै ।

ई आपदा प्रभावित क्षेत्र आरू आसपास के जलवायु परिस्थिति के नियमित विश्लेषण भी तैयार करलकै, साथ ही साथ विस्तारित रेंज के पूर्वानुमान भी कई सप्ताह आगू देखै छै ।

सीएमए के समन्वय में राष्ट्रीय जलवायु केन्द्र नेपाल के दू मुख्य श्रेणी के उत्पाद उपलब्ध करा रहल अछि -- जलवायु निगरानी आ जलवायु पूर्वानुमान ।

जलवायु निगरानी कें लेल इ केंद्र पांच प्रकार कें नियमित उत्पादक कें उत्पादन करयत छै जे तापमान, वर्षा आ मिट्टी कें सूखा जैना परिस्थितिक कें कवर करयत छै. ई 10 प्रमुख जलवायु सूचकऽ क॑ भी ट्रैक करै छै, जेकरा म॑ एल नीनो-दक्षिणी दोलन या एनएसओ, आरू मैडेन-जूलियन दोलन या एमजेओ शामिल छै ।

एनएसओ प्राकृतिक जलवायु चक्र क॑ कहलऽ जाय छै जे दुनिया भर के मौसम क॑ प्रभावित करै छै । एहि मे गर्म एल नीनो चरण आ ठंडा ला नीना चरण शामिल अछि । एनएसओ के विपरीत जे स्थिर छै, एमजेओ बादल, वर्षा, हवा, आरू दबाव केरऽ पूर्व तरफ बढ़ै वाला गड़बड़ी छै जे उष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्रऽ क॑ पार करी क॑ औसतन ३० स॑ ६० दिन म॑ अपनऽ प्रारंभिक बिंदु प॑ वापस आबी जाय छै ।

title: ‘Gone in a blink’: Nepal floods sweep away Indian workers who built hotels - Al Jazeera
description: ‘Gone in a blink’: Nepal floods sweep away Indian workers who built hotels  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Bettiah, India – Neyaz Miya was adjusting a kitchen handle. Mehadi Hassan was fixing a bracket for a bed.

They were at different construction sites – Miya in a half‑constructed home, a little higher up the hill, while Hassan was on the ground floor of Ganesh Hotel, closer to the Trishuli River that flowed through Syafrubesi, a bustling market town near the Nepal‑Tibet border, now wiped off the map by the August 26 flash floods.

More than 1,200 bodies have been recovered since then, at least 4,000 people remain missing, and more than 13,000 have been rescued.

“First came the terrifying loud sound. Then the ground trembled, and dark clouds descended upon us,” recalls 34‑year‑old Miya, who ran further up the hill with his phone and slippers that morning, five or six others running alongside him.

Hassan, lower on the slope, did not wait to reach for his slippers or his phone. He just ran, climbing a narrow, stair‑like path, up the hill, stopping only when he reached roughly 60 metres (200ft) above the road.

At some point, Miya and Hassan found each other. Around them were 60 to 70 other survivors who had also gathered high up on the hill.

A decade earlier, Miya had arrived in Syafrubesi as a carpenter. Three years later, he brought Hassan with him – both men from Bihar’s Bettiah district. Over the years, they built the town’s interiors – sofas, beds, almirahs, and kitchens for hotels and homes.

On that Wednesday morning, they watched all of that washed away. The multi‑storey hotels where they had worked – Red Panda, Garden Hotel, Buddha Hotel, Sunrise Hotel – were all swallowed by the flood.

Advertisement

“The town was gone in a blink,” Miya recounts, now sitting in his home in Turhapatti village of Bihar, India, just across the Nepal border. “There were only three kinds of people who survived that day: Those who were out of town, those who were at work and managed to run, and those who lived a little higher up the hill.”

Based on what he witnessed, Miya says only a few hundred people in Syafrubesi, a town that had a population of 2,271 in the 2011 census, likely survived.

Miya and Hasan are among them. Three of their close friends and colleagues, also migrant workers from Bihar, are not.

Neyaz Miya (far right), with his wife Rijwana Khatun, his mother Rubaida Khatun, and his father Doshahmad Miya. Neyaz survived the floods, but lost his masonry tools, worth almost $1000 [Jyoti Yadav/Al Jazeera]

A workday like no other

When the floods reached Syafrubesi, the men were already at work: Their shifts began at seven in the morning.

“To start at seven, we would wake up at four or five,” Miya recalls. They would leave with empty stomachs and were fed tea with doughnuts or biscuits at the construction site by building owners. Their first break came at 11am, when they returned to the rented one‑room space (3,500 Nepali rupees or $23 a month) that housed five to seven migrants at a time.

On the morning of August 26, they left for work alongside 34‑year‑old Arman Ansari, 20‑year‑old Samir Ansari, and 52‑year‑old Mukhtar Ansari, all migrants from Miya’s Turhapatti village.

In the rented room, two teenage boys, Arman’s 14‑year‑old son, Salman Alam, and his friend Shibu Alam, 17, remained asleep. They had come a month earlier to visit the hills.

“My father had cooked meat bhaat (rice with meat),” Salman recounts. He was waiting for his father to return at 11am so they could eat together.

Arman, his father, was working beside Hassan on the ground floor, pasting sunmica onto the same bed. Samir and Mukhtar were on the top floor of the Full Moon Hotel.

When Hassan ran out of the under-construction building and up the hill, he believed Arman was behind him. But by the time Hassan and Miya met higher up, there was no sign of the other three: Arman, Samir and Mukhtar.

Miya and Hassan found the boys, Salman and Shibu, terrified, on the hill. “Salman was crying, howling and searching for his father,” Hassan said.

The flood, which came with a high speed, took half an hour to recede. Soon, helicopters started hovering above them, airlifting the critically injured.

The four of them – Miya, Hassan and the boys – walked down the hill on foot to search for the three missing in the debris. They found nothing but sludge. Miya’s furniture-cutting tools and machines, worth 80,000 Nepali rupees ($530), were buried in the debris.

Advertisement

When they got back to their room, perched high on a slope, they found that it had survived.

But the army had taken charge, and soldiers herded survivors away from tenements near the river. “They said it [the flood] might come again,” Miya recalls.

They slept that night in a government school building in a village, he says. “At night, we were given daal bhat (rice and daal), and we wrapped ourselves in tarpaulin and slept.”

The next morning, a helicopter took them to another village. From there, another helicopter carried them to an army compound in a town. In the evening, they teamed up with five other migrants and hired an SUV to reach Nepal’s capital Kathmandu, each paying 3,500 rupees ($23).

The next morning, on August 28, they hired another SUV, which charged them 950 rupees ($6) each for a distance of 290km (180 miles) to Birgunj, a town on the India-Nepal border. They then crossed the border on foot before boarding buses for their villages.

It wasn’t the homecoming Indian migrants who work in Nepal usually plan.

A lane in Turhapatti village, Bihar, India, where the migrant workers are from. It is a village where almost every family has a story of migration [Jyoti Yadav/Al Jazeera]

‘No regular work’ back home

Turhapatti is among thousands of villages tucked along the 1,715km (1,066-mile) stretch of the India-Nepal border, where generations have crossed back and forth in search of work.

The two countries share an open border, and on both sides, especially in Bihar, the bond is known as a roti-beti ka rishta (a relationship of food and daughters), alluding to ties of livelihoods and matrimonial kinship. People live, work, and marry across the border.

Kathmandu is as close to Turhapatti as is Patna, the capital of Bihar. Per its 2021 Population and Housing Census, Nepal had 700,000 foreign-born residents, 97 percent of them from India.

Miya and Hassan say the wages for a carpenter or a mason on the Indian side are between 600-700 rupees, while for the same work in Nepal, wages are about 900 rupees. That drives migrant workers from India over the border into Nepal.

Nepal, for its part, is facing a major out-migration crisis — its per capita income is the lowest in South Asia, barring Afghanistan, and hundreds of thousands of young men and women leave each year to find work elsewhere. This creates a demand for migrant workers from Bihar, India’s poorest state that lies just across the border.

In Turhapatti, Miya owns only 0.03 hectares (0.06 acres), not enough to feed his family of six children, wife and parents. In recent years, he transitioned from being a carpenter to a contractor, which allowed him to bring in more workers from Bihar.

He had been sending 30,000 Indian rupees ($315) back to his family every month.

Hassan has even less back home: He inherited a 6×8-metre (20×25ft) room from his father and no agricultural land. “There is no regular daily work here,” he says. He would send 15,000 Indian rupees ($157) home from Nepal each month for his wife and four children.

Advertisement

Their story echoes in most homes in Turhapatti. The village had a population of 16,000 people in the 2011 census, India’s latest one. In nearly every household, men have left to work in other parts of India and abroad as carpenters, masons, or labourers mixing cement and sand into mortar.

The destinations are Kashmir, where close to 700 men from the village work; Nepal, with nearly 600; and thousands scattered across Indian cities: Chennai, Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai. About 100 men have migrated to Dubai, Oman and Saudi Arabia.

The houses they built in Turhapatti stand in stark contrast to those of those who remain in India. The marble-fronted and iron-gated homes belong to men working in the Gulf, while semi-permanent dwellings belong to those who stayed behind.

Migrants in Nepal fall in between: Miya has been able to raise a brick house.

Sahrun Khatun, Arman’s wife, with her eldest son Salman (holding the youngest child) who survived, her mother-in-law, and two younger children, outside their home in Turhapatti, Bihar, India [Jyoti Yadav/Al Jazeera]

‘My body shivers at the thought’

This economic reality is what drove Arman Ansari to Syafrubesi. On July 26, Arman left for Nepal with Samir and Mukhtar. Arman’s son and his friend Shubu went with the three adults; the teenagers were on a trip to the hills.

Now, Arman’s brother-in-law. Jameel Miya, a carpenter in Kathmandu, scours the city’s hospitals for Arman’s body, telling authorities that his brother-in-law’s right hand and chest had deep scars, cut by shards of glass when he was young.

Arman’s wife, Sahrun Khatun, has only her last phone call with Arman to hold on to. They spoke two hours before the floods swept him away. “He was about to get his wages on September 1 and return home,” she says.

Salman, who had tagged along with his father to see the hills, hasn’t been able to sleep since the flood.

“The moment I close my eyes, I feel the flood is coming for me,” he says.

Mukhtar’s family lives a few lanes away.

Since the floods, Kasmun Khatun, Mukhtar’s wife, has been glued to the internet for any news of her missing husband. Joining her in that remote search are her daughter Asmana (18) and son Sadre Alam (14).

Her eldest son, Osama, 25, a tailor in Kathmandu, has been busy searching for his father in city hospitals.

“After waiting for a week and watching the videos, I submitted my DNA samples,” he says over a phone call. Osama manages to send home 6,000 rupees ($63), but that is no longer enough – his mother needs eye surgery that has already been delayed and cannot be put off much longer.

“The guardian has gone, all of a sudden,” he says, referring to his father.

At the far edge of Turhapatti stands the home of Samir Ansari, the youngest among the missing migrants and youngest of his five migrant brothers.

The Ganesh Hotel project he was working on was only three days from completion.

“He said he found another site to work on,” recalls his father, Hasmuddin Miya, remembering their last phone call on the evening of August 25.

Samir was a mason who specialised in marble tiles, a skill he had learned in Kashmir while working under his elder brothers at construction sites.

The three families are preparing to host a bhoj, the funeral feast – a custom of feeding hundreds of people – having given up on hope.

Meanwhile, the two survivors, Miya and Hassan, are already making calls to find work again. This time, their search turns towards Nepal’s plains. They pledge never to return to the hills.

“My whole body shivers at the thought of going there,” says Hassan.

बेतिया, भारत – नेयाज मिया एकटा किचन हैंडल एडजस्ट क’ रहल छलीह. मेहादी हसन एकटा पलंगक लेल ब्रैकेट ठीक क’ रहल छलाह।

ओ सब अलग-अलग निर्माण स्थल पर छल – मिया आधा निर्मित घर में, पहाड़ी सं कनेक ऊँच, जखन कि हसन गणेश होटल के भूतल पर, त्रिशुली नदी के नजदीक जे नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा के पास एकटा चहल-पहल वाला बाजार शहर स्याफ्रूबेसी सं बहैत छल, जे आब 26 अगस्त के आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सं नक्शा सं मिटा गेल छल.

तहिया सं 1200 सं बेसि लाश बरामद भ चुकल अछि, कम सं कम 4000 लोक लापता अछि, आओर 13 हजार सं बेसि लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि.

34 वर्षीय मिया मोन पाड़ैत छथि, "पहिने भयावह तेज आवाज आयल। तखन जमीन काँपि उठल, आ कारी मेघ हमरा सभ पर उतरि गेल।"

ढलान पर नीचाँ हसन अपन चप्पल आ ने फोन दिस हाथ बढ़ेबाक प्रतीक्षा नहि केलक। ओ बस दौड़ल, एकटा संकीर्ण, सीढ़ी सन बाट पर चढ़ि, पहाड़ी पर चढ़ि, तखनहि रुकि गेल जखन ओ सड़क सं मोटा-मोटी 60 मीटर (200फीट) ऊपर पहुँचि गेल.

कोनो समय मिया आ हसन एक दोसरा के पाबि गेल। हुनका सब के चारू कात 60 स 70 अन्य बचि गेल लोक सेहो छल जे पहाड़ी पर ऊँच ऊपर जमा भ गेल छल।

एक दशक पहिने मिया बढ़ई बनि स्याफ्रूबेसी पहुँचल छलीह । तीन साल बाद ओ हसन केँ संग अनलनि – दुनू आदमी बिहारक बेतिया जिलाक। वर्षों में शहर के इंटीरियर – सोफा, बेड, अल्मिरा, आ होटल आ घर के लेल किचन बनौलनि.

ओहि बुध दिन भोरे ओ सभ ओहि सबटा केँ बहैत देखैत रहलाह। जाहि बहुमंजिला होटल मे ओ लोकनि काज केने छलाह – रेड पांडा, गार्डन होटल, बुद्ध होटल, सनराइज होटल – सबटा बाढ़ि मे निगल गेल छल.

विज्ञापन

आब नेपाल सीमाक ठीक ओहि पार भारतक बिहारक तुरहापट्टी गाम मे अपन घर मे बैसल मिया बतबैत छथि, “कस्बा पलक झपकैत चलि गेल छल। “ओहि दिन तीन तरहक लोक बचल छल: जे शहरसँ बाहर छल, जे काज पर छल आ दौड़बामे सफल भ’ गेल छल, आ जे पहाड़ीसँ कनेक ऊँच रहैत छल।”

जे किछु देखलनि ओकर आधार पर मिया कहैत छथि जे 2011 क जनगणना मे 2271 क आबादी वाला शहर स्याफ्रूबेसी मे मात्र किछु सौ लोक बचल हेबाक संभावना अछि।

मिया आ हसन सेहो ओहि मे शामिल छथि। हुनकर तीनटा घनिष्ठ मित्र आ सहयोगी जे बिहार स प्रवासी मजदूर सेहो छथि, एहन नहि छथि।

नेयाज मिया (सबसँ दाहिना), पत्नी रिजवाना खातून, माय रुबैदा खातून, आ पिता दोषहमद मियाक संग। नेयाज बाढ़ि स बचि गेल, मुदा चिनाई क औजार गंवा देलक, जेकर कीमत लगभग 1000 डॉलर छल [ज्योति यादव/अल जजीरा]।

एकटा एहन काजक दिन जेना कोनो आन दिन नहि

बाढ़ि जखन स्याफ्रुबेसी पहुँचल तखन पुरुष लोकनि पहिने सँ काज पर छलाह : भोर मे सात बजे सँ पाली शुरू भ' गेलनि।

मिया स्मरण करैत कहैत छथि जे सात बजे स शुरू करबा लेल हम सब चारि-पांच बजे उठैत छलहुं। खाली पेट चलि जाइत छलाह आ भवन मालिक द्वारा निर्माण स्थल पर डोनट वा बिस्कुटक संग चाह खुआओल जाइत छल । हुनका लोकनिक पहिल ब्रेक 11 बजे भेलनि, जखन ओ लोकनि किराया पर एक कमराक जगह (3500 नेपाली रुपैया वा 23 डॉलर महीना) पर वापस आबि गेलाह जाहि मे एक बेर मे पांच सं सात टा प्रवासी रहैत छलाह.

The Emirati search and rescue team, which arrived in the Himalayan country on September 4, joined forces with Nepali authorities to carry out the mission in the Trishuli area.

title: The questions China won’t answer about the Tibet-Nepal flood disaster - asiatimes.com
description: The questions China won’t answer about the Tibet-Nepal flood disaster  asiatimes.com
publisher.title: asiatimes.com
full_article:
For years, analysts and observers have warned about the dangers of China’s relentless infrastructure push in Tibet, particularly its dam-building ambitions on the Brahmaputra River, known in China as the Yarlung Tsangpo.

Beijing has repeatedly waved away such concerns, insisting it has conducted feasibility studies and environmental impact assessments. But its actions on the ground in the Himalayas have told a different story.

For India, the concern is not merely that it sits downstream. Rather, it is the sheer scale of infrastructure being built in one of the world’s most ecologically fragile and sensitive regions.

The Himalayas were never meant to be another frontier for construction, development and militarization. India has long understood that disrupting such a delicate ecosystem can have devastating consequences downstream. That warning can no longer be dismissed as hypothetical.

On August 26, flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border thrust the ecological consequences of China’s Himalayan infrastructure expansion into devastating view. The floods have since claimed thousands of lives across multiple countries, including more than 350 Indians, most of them pilgrims on the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a Hindu holy pilgrimage.

The full toll — in lives and economic damage — remains unknown. But the immediate question is whether this can be dismissed as a natural disaster triggered solely by natural causes. The answer is far more complicated than a straightforward yes.

This is not an attempt to politicize a tragedy. It is precisely because lives have been lost that hard questions must be asked. What role did human intervention play? Did infrastructure development alter the landscape or worsen the consequences? And, most importantly, what can be done to prevent similar tragedies?

Is China culpable?

Dismissing the floods, which video reports show crashing dramatically at Tibet’s Gyirong Port, as purely a natural disaster would be a disservice both to those who lost their lives and to the fragile environment of the region. There is little doubt that China should accept some level of accountability.

For years, Beijing has pursued the so-called development and modernization of Tibet through an aggressive infrastructure buildout. Dams, highways, tunnels and railways are rising across Tibet, while similar projects are being pushed into Nepal. One particularly consequential example is the $167 billion hydropower system now under construction in Tibet.

The international community, however, has failed to respond to these developments or adequately assess their consequences. But Tibet is too fragile to be relentlessly reshaped by Chinese military and infrastructure ambitions.

The common official narrative emerging from China, as reflected in the state-run Global Times, is that “today’s natural disasters are chain reactions driven by the superposition of climate change, geological vulnerability, cross-border watershed risks and infrastructure exposure.”

There is also the issue of information control. Reports say Chinese authorities are censoring videos of the floods online, and many accounts on the Chinese internet have cast calls for accountability as information warfare against China.

That is hardly a constructive response. Beijing’s message after the tragedy was “people first, life first” — but such rhetoric means little without transparency and accountability.

What’s the solution?

The straightforward solution is to halt further infrastructure development in Tibet. But this is not an issue confined to Tibet — its consequences extend to every country that shares a border with it.

Treating the floods as a one-off tragedy would be a mistake; they may be only an initial warning of what lies ahead. Once again, Tibet has returned to the world’s attention — a region whose religious and cultural suppression the international community has long chosen to ignore.

But can it afford to ignore the ecological damage that so-called infrastructure development may cause or worsen?

Even if China blames climate change, human activity is known to accelerate climate-driven risks. Addressing disasters of this nature requires collective effort — and collective effort, in turn, requires transparency and respect for the Himalayas and their natural environment.

The lesson here is that some places must be left alone — particularly the ecologically sensitive and fragile Himalayas. When nations refuse to respect nature’s limits, nature eventually responds, sometimes in the form of a disaster that could have been averted.

The still largely unexplained floodwaters that crashed through Tibet’s Gyirong Port and then downstream through Nepal, leaving behind a still unknown number of casualties in their wake, are a warning the world must take seriously.

Rahul Mishra is an Associate Professor at the Centre for Indo-Pacific Studies, School of International Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, and a Senior Research Fellow at the German–Southeast Asian Center of Excellence for Public Policy and Good Governance, Thammasat University, Thailand. की चीन दोषी अछि ?

मुदा की ओ पारिस्थितिकी के नुकसान के अनदेखी करय के सामर्थ्य राखि सकैत अछि जे तथाकथित बुनियादी ढांचा के विकास सं भ सकैत अछि या खराब भ सकैत अछि?

अखनी तलक बहुत हद तक अस्पष्ट बाढ़ के पानी जे तिब्बत केरऽ ग्यिरोंग बंदरगाह स॑ होय क॑ आरू ओकरा बाद नेपाल के रास्ता स॑ नीचें गिरी गेलै, जेकरा म॑ अखनी तलक अज्ञात संख्या म॑ जानमाल के नुकसान होय ​​गेलै, ई एगो चेतावनी छै जेकरा दुनिया क॑ गंभीरता स॑ लेना चाहियऽ ।

full_article:
Key Takeaways Climate impacts are reshaping bilateral ties, as the Nepal - China flash flood from unstable Himalayan glaciers exposed border vulnerabilities.

- flash flood from unstable exposed border vulnerabilities. China 's overseas climate aid is shifting from hardware to technology and expertise, notably its satellite and forecasting early warning systems.

's overseas climate aid is shifting from hardware to technology and expertise, notably its satellite and forecasting early warning systems. The disaster exposed sensitive tensions over responsibility: Nepal's brief call for climate compensation highlighted disputes over climate justice .

On August 26, 2026, a sudden collapse of ice and rock unleashed a catastrophic flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river valleys, devastating northern Nepal and spilling across the border into Tibet. Villages were wiped out, bridges and roads destroyed, and hydropower stations wrecked. The death toll was severe, and will likely rise further as many remain unaccounted.

The episode has thrust China’s climate impact response with the Global South into the spotlight as never before. It also crystallizes several trends that have been building for years.

The first is that climate change has outgrown its role as a purely multilateral diplomatic issue for China. It’s increasingly woven into bilateral relationships, especially with neighboring states. The Nepal border disaster, rooted in long-term warming and the resulting instability of Himalayan glaciers, is a stark case study in how climate impacts can directly affect a border relationship. A similar dynamic is unfolding in Southeast Asia, where a warming climate is intensifying flood and drought risk across the Mekong basin, pushing China and downstream nations toward closer coordination on disaster response, early warning, and water management.

Second, the disaster illustrates the need for a shift in how China delivers climate assistance overseas. Where China’s support once centered on hardware (such as solar panels, solar water heaters, solar streetlights), it has increasingly moved toward offering technology, expertise, and platforms. In recent years, China has become a significant supplier of early-warning systems internationally, pairing its satellite and forecasting capabilities with data gathered on the ground in partner countries to improve disaster prediction. The Nepal disaster has brought new urgency to accelerating this approach.

Third, the fallout reveals a delicate position China occupies in climate responsibilities vis-à-vis Global South countries. Nepal initially called for “climate compensation” from China, the US, and India, invoking the language of climate justice. This demand immediately drew outsized attention because China is simultaneously a major polluter, Nepal’s neighbor, and a self-considered developing country. By September 3, however, Nepal had quickly walked back the request, claiming, in a meeting between its Foreign Minister and China’s ambassador to Nepal, that it would instead pursue support through existing multilateral climate channels.

That reversal captures the interesting tension at play. As climate change becomes more entangled with China’s relationships with its developing country neighbors, questions of climate responsibility and compensation remain a highly sensitive topic. Beijing is undoubtedly very wary of any precedent tying its emitter status to direct compensation claims.

Taken together, the Nepal-China disaster may be a preview of things to come. As climate impacts grow more severe, they’re likely to become a permanent and expanding thread in China’s relations with Global South nations. This will certainly bring both new frictions and new cooperation opportunities.

26 अगस्त 2026 क॑ अचानक बर्फ आरू चट्टान केरऽ ढहला स॑ भोटे कोशी आरू त्रिशुली नदी केरऽ घाटी के नीचें भयावह फ्लैश फ्लड पैदा होय गेलै, जेकरा स॑ उत्तरी नेपाल क॑ तबाह करी देलऽ गेलै आरू सीमा पार करी क॑ तिब्बत म॑ फैललऽ गेलै । गाम-गाम सफाया भ गेल, पुल आ सड़क तबाह भ गेल, आ जलविद्युत स्टेशन ध्वस्त भ गेल। मृतक केरऽ संख्या गंभीर छेलै, आरू संभव छै कि आरू बढ़ी जैतै, कैन्हेंकि बहुत लोगऽ के हिसाब-किताब नै छै ।

ई एपिसोड न॑ चीन केरऽ ग्लोबल साउथ के साथ जलवायु प्रभाव प्रतिक्रिया क॑ ऐन्हऽ तरह स॑ चर्चा म॑ लानल॑ छै जेतना कि पहलऽ कहियो नै छेलै । ई कतेको एहन प्रवृत्ति के सेहो क्रिस्टलीकृत करैत अछि जे सालों स बनैत आबि रहल अछि।

पहिल ई छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन चीन लेली विशुद्ध बहुपक्षीय कूटनीतिक मुद्दा के रूप म॑ अपनऽ भूमिका स॑ आगू बढ़ी गेलऽ छै । ई तेजी स॑ द्विपक्षीय संबंधऽ म॑ बुनलऽ छै, खास करी क॑ पड़ोसी राज्यऽ के साथ । दीर्घकालीन गर्मी आरू एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप हिमालयी ग्लेशियर केरऽ अस्थिरता म॑ जड़ जमाय वाला नेपाल सीमा आपदा ई बात केरऽ एगो शुद्ध केस स्टडी छै कि जलवायु केरऽ प्रभाव सीमा संबंध क॑ कोना सीधा प्रभावित करी सकै छै । दक्षिण पूर्व एशिया म॑ भी ऐसनऽ ही गतिशीलता खुली रहलऽ छै, जहां गर्म होय रहलऽ जलवायु के कारण पूरा मेकांग बेसिन म॑ बाढ़ आरू सूखा के खतरा तेज होय रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ चीन आरू नीचे के राष्ट्रऽ क॑ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया, पूर्व चेतावनी आरू जल प्रबंधन प॑ करीबी समन्वय के तरफ धकेललऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

दोसर, ई आपदा चीन विदेशऽ म॑ जलवायु सहायता केना पहुँचै छै, एकरा म॑ बदलाव के जरूरत क॑ दर्शाबै छै । जहाँ चीन केरऽ समर्थन कहियो हार्डवेयर (जैना कि सोलर पैनल, सोलर वॉटर हीटर, सोलर स्ट्रीटलाइट) प॑ केंद्रित छेलै, वहीं चीन केरऽ तेजी स॑ तकनीक, विशेषज्ञता, आरू प्लेटफॉर्म पेश करै के तरफ बढ़ी गेलऽ छै । हाल के सालऽ म॑ चीन अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर प॑ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली केरऽ एगो महत्वपूर्ण आपूर्तिकर्ता बनी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ आपदा के भविष्यवाणी म॑ सुधार लेली अपनऽ उपग्रह आरू पूर्वानुमान क्षमता क॑ साझेदार देशऽ म॑ जमीन प॑ एकत्रित करलऽ गेलऽ आंकड़ऽ के साथ जोड़लऽ गेलऽ छै । नेपाल आपदा एहि दृष्टिकोण केँ तेज करबाक नव तात्कालिकता अनलक अछि ।

तेसरऽ, एकरऽ परिणाम स॑ पता चलै छै कि चीन केरऽ जलवायु जिम्मेदारी म॑ ग्लोबल साउथ देशऽ के सामने एगो नाजुक स्थिति छै । नेपाल शुरू मे जलवायु न्याय के भाषा के आह्वान करैत चीन, अमेरिका, आ भारत स “जलवायु मुआवजा” के आह्वान केलक । ई मांग तुरंत आउटसाइज के ध्यान आकर्षित करलकै, कैन्हेंकि चीन एक साथ एगो प्रमुख प्रदूषक, नेपाल के पड़ोसी, आरू एक स्वंगणित विकासशील देश छै । लेकिन ३ सितम्बर तलक नेपाल न॑ जल्दी स॑ ई आग्रह क॑ वापस करी क॑ अपनऽ विदेश मंत्री आरू नेपाल म॑ चीन केरऽ राजदूत के बीच एगो बैठक म॑ दावा करलकै कि वू एकरऽ बदला म॑ मौजूदा बहुपक्षीय जलवायु चैनलऽ के माध्यम स॑ समर्थन के पीछा करतै ।

ओ उलटफेर खेल मे रोचक तनाव केँ पकड़ि लैत अछि । जेना-जेना जलवायु परिवर्तन चीन केरऽ अपनऽ विकासशील देशऽ के पड़ोसी देशऽ के साथ संबंधऽ स॑ उलझलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जलवायु जिम्मेदारी आरू मुआवजा के सवाल एगो बेहद संवेदनशील विषय बनलऽ छै । निस्संदेह बीजिंग अपनऽ एमिटर केरऽ दर्जा क॑ सीधा मुआवजा के दावा स॑ जोड़ै वाला कोनो भी मिसाल स॑ बहुत सावधान छै ।

एकरा मिला कए नेपाल-चीन आपदा आबै बला चीजक पूर्वावलोकन भ सकैत अछि । जेना-जेना जलवायु केरऽ प्रभाव बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, संभावना छै कि ई ग्लोबल साउथ राष्ट्रऽ के साथ चीन केरऽ संबंधऽ म॑ एगो स्थायी आरू विस्तारित धागा बनी जैतै । एहि स निश्चित रूप स नव घर्षण आ नव सहयोग क अवसर दुनू भेटत।

The recent floods in Nepal have raised fresh questions about China’s construction activity in Tibet. Mr Tsewang Dorji, Research Fellow at the Tibet Policy Institute, pointed out on the Gist that China has expanded roads, railways, airports and military infrastructure across Tibet, including in ecologically fragile areas close to India, Nepal and Bhutan.

He argues that Chinese infrastructure requires changing the patterns of nature, such as building railways by cutting mountains and creating dams on rivers. “Besides, China has also censored all the news and information and produced its own narrative around the recent flood, pointing towards how the situation in Nepal and Tibet is not a natural disaster.”

Dr Y Nithiyanandam, head of the Geospatial program at the Takshashila Institution, drew a more careful comparison between the construction and the latest disaster. He said that 3D assessment points to a glacial and slope failure that sent a mass of ice and debris into the valley. While the primary assessment points out that the natural disaster could be due to climate change, he cautions that much longer observation is required before attributing it to just nature.

He further adds that satellite imagery and remote sensing can only show where terrain is shifting and where new construction is appearing. However, it cannot be predicted precisely when a slope will give way. Nithiyanandam said that kind of assessment needs long-term ground monitoring alongside observations from space — difficult when access inside Tibet is restricted.

The restricted access also acts a blind spot in several other infrastructure projects created by China that may impact its neighbours, India included. The Medog dam is one of them.

Dorji highlights that China is building its giant hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo, in a vulnerable terrain exposed to earthquakes and landslides. Beijing continues to press ahead despite repeated environmental warnings. He adds that such development in Tibet will impact India’s environmental ecosystem too as the Himalayas are the lungs of India. However, Dorji adds, for China, “destruction is nothing,” following Mao’s and the Chinese Communist Party’s political slogan that ‘man must conquer nature’.

Dr Nithiyanandam adds that the dam can lead to changes in snowfall, surface water and river behaviour across the Tibetan Plateau. Upstream alterations can pose further risks to downstream ecosystems and livelihoods, long before their cause becomes easy to establish or ends up getting attributed to ‘climate change’.

While India can watch much of this construction in Tibet from space, the next concern for New Delhi is how to manage these changes in the Himalayas when they pose this level of risk to life and property. Although both experts warn that local voices remain unheard, they point out that the ecological aspect needs to be measured.
